issues.issue: The clause makes coverage turn on the Company "designated by [an] 'X' in the box below," but no mark appears on the face of the certificate and only one carrier name is printed, so which company actually undertook the risk is left to construction. That matters because the related release runs to American Guarantee and Liability Insurance Company and its affiliates rather than to the Zurich entity printed here.

The certificate declares a "claims made and reported" trigger but supplies no definition of "Claim" or of when a claim is "made," content that exists only in the "Master Policy" invoked by Item 7, Item 8 and the issuance clause. The trigger therefore cannot be applied from this instrument alone.

The reporting condition depends on the "Certificate Period" fixed in Item 5 and on "any applicable extended reporting period," but Item 5's dates are unreadable ("2/45/2007" to "2/AS/2808") and no extended reporting period terms appear anywhere in the certificate, which sends the reader to the Master Policy referenced in Items 7 and 8. The outer boundary of the reporting obligation thus cannot be determined from this document.

"Reported in writing to the Company" does not say whether written notice given to the Producer named in Item 3 (Insurance Specialties Services, Inc.) or to the program administrator satisfies the condition. The phrase "first made and reported" is likewise silent on whether both events must fall inside the same period.

"Defense Costs" is placed in quotation marks as a defined term, but the certificate contains no definition; its content comes only from the Master Policy invoked by Item 8 and the issuance clause. What sums fall outside the Item 4 limits is therefore not determinable from the certificate.

Item 1 names only the individual Jonathan D. Rosen as "Named Certificate Holder," while Item 2 extends additional-insured status to corporate entities and Item 4 measures limits "Each Named Certificate Holder"; read together, the certificate never says whether Rosen's agency or corporate entities are insured or in what capacity he is covered. That gap is what decides whether corporate claimants have coverage at all.

"the Registered Representatives of ProEquities" designates an unnamed and shifting class of additional insureds with no list, effective date or capacity limitation, and the neighbouring names are incomplete ("Empire General"). Whether a given person or entity falls inside that class cannot be answered from the words used.

The each-claim limit is printed as "$2,060,000,09" against a stated aggregate of "$2,000,000.00," so on its face the per-claim figure is both nonsensical in punctuation and larger than the aggregate. A court would have to decide what the per-claim limit is.

The Certificate Period is expressed as "2/45/2007 To 12:01 A.M. on 2/AS/2808" — an impossible day and an unreadable end date — so the policy's inception and expiry cannot be read off the instrument. Every claims-made and reporting condition keys to this period.

The $500 tier applies to "products of Protective Life and ProEquities, Inc." without saying whether "and" is conjunctive, and "products" is undefined, while the residual "all other covered products" is a catch-all whose reach is fixed only by the specific names in the first tier. Which deductible attaches to a mixed or third-party product claim is therefore open.

The premium — the consideration for the coverage — is not stated but left to the "Master Policy," a document neither attached nor described, which sits awkwardly with the closing clause stating that "this policy embodies all agreements" between the holder and the Company. The amount and payment terms cannot be found within the four corners of the certificate.

Item 8 leaves the endorsements effective at inception unidentified by referring to the Master Policy, so unnamed endorsements may qualify the certificate's own statements about limits, defense costs and the reporting condition. That collides with the closing clause's assertion that this policy embodies all agreements between the holder and the Company.

This clause subordinates the certificate to a "Master Policy" issued to Insurance Professionals Protection Group, Inc. that is not attached, yet the very next sentence declares that this policy embodies all agreements between the Named Certificate Holder and the Company. Which document controls, and whether master policy terms and conditions bind the certificate holder, is left unresolved.

The clause converts "the statements in the 'Certificate of Insurance' and the application and any attachments hereto" into the holder's own representations, but no application or attachment is identified or annexed to the certificate. Which writings the holder is deemed to have warranted, for misrepresentation or rescission purposes, cannot be determined from the text.

The integration sentence is truncated — it ends "relating to this" with no object — so the subject matter over which it claims to be exhaustive is missing from the instrument. A court would have to supply the cut-off words before the clause can be applied.

The declaration that this policy embodies all agreements cannot be squared with the preceding issuance clause making the certificate subject to the "Master Policy," nor with Items 7 and 8, which supply premium and endorsements only by reference to that outside document. The clause and those cross-references pull in opposite directions on what constitutes the contract.
